messages:
OpsBot: [ALERT] gpu-pool-west-2 queue length spike (90th=480s), autoscaler failed to provision new nodes (error: quota/exceeded). Paging oncall.
Leah Park: paging now. seeing lots of CUDA Xid messages in node logs, OOMs on driver, nodes flapping in last 6m. customers in west-eu and us-west affected. :rotating_light:
Sanjay Iyer: oncall here. looking at metrics — queue size up 9x, token throughput down 60%. autoscaler logs show repeated 'scale failed: driver registration timeout' from the runtime agent.
Maddy Chen: grabbing node logs. seeing repeated kernel-oom and nv_peer_mem errors + Xid 31/42 churn. suspect a driver leak after recent kernel+driver build we rolled last night.
Leah Park: who rolled the driver? @maddy any canary traffic? we need to know blast radius and whether Dedicated pools are impacted.
Maddy Chen: we did a constrained rollout to west regions, rollout id: rollout/2026-03-12-driver-rt. Canary showed minor errors but not this scale. Looks like memory fragmentation / persistent allocations causing node signals under load.
Sanjay Iyer: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pause autoscaler (it's trying and failing, amplifying churn). 2) Remove problem nodes from rotation (cordon & drain) so runtime won't schedule new jobs on flapping nodes. 3) Spawn replacement nodes using last-known-good driver image. 4) Temporarily increase reserved capacity for customer-critical Pools. 5) Inform product/support about customer impact.
Leah Park: do it. I'll open an incidents->postmortem ticket and start a customer-impact note. Which pools to prioritize? top customers on Dedicated: acme, orbit, prisma.
Maddy Chen: executing cordon/drain on flapping hosts list (flap-ids from agent): n-gpu-132, n-gpu-137, n-gpu-140.
Maddy Chen: running:
```
kubectl cordon n-gpu-132 && kubectl drain n-gpu-132 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
# repeat for 137,140
```
Maddy Chen: also restarting driver daemonset on replacements with image tag `driver:v2026-03-10-stable` (rollback to canary-last-known-good).
Sanjay Iyer: paused autoscaler via infra CLI:
```
infra autoscaler update --pool gpu-pool-west-2 --enabled false
```
OpsBot: action taken: autoscaler paused by @Sanjay Iyer at 1718501300. Reaction :white_check_mark:
Leah Park: customer impact: elevated 5xxs and slow responses for embeddings/generation routes for several customers in region. Support pinged and triaged. We should prepare an incident banner for affected customers.
Maddy Chen: replacements coming up. New nodes booting with good image. I'm also increasing kube-scheduler eviction threshold to avoid immediate OOM eviction thrash while we stabilize.
Sanjay Iyer: temporarily bumped reserved capacity for dedicated pools (acme-prd +20 GPUs) and set routing policy to prefer eu-central fallback for traffic from west. This will increase latency for those requests but avoid 503s.
Leah Park: good. @PagerDuty can you escalate to platform eng for driver rollback verification and probe if there are kernel-level fixes pending?
PagerDuty: escalation sent to eng-platform oncall.
Maddy Chen: live logs show Xid stream dropping after drain + restart on replacements. Old flapping nodes still showing OOMs, will decommission them and attach to debug pool for deeper analysis.
Leah Park: notify support: draft message — "We detected a GPU driver instability in west region causing increased errors and higher latency. We’ve paused autoscaling, drained affected hosts, and rolled back to a stable driver image. Traffic is being routed to fallback regions and reserved capacity has been increased for critical customers. We are monitoring and will update in 30 mins." Approve?
Sanjay Iyer: approve. send now, include mitigations and ETA ~30-45m for full recovery.
OpsBot: sent customer banner to affected accounts at 1718501425.
Maddy Chen: quick note on root cause hypothesis: new driver had a memory accounting regression that under high concurrency prevents KV cache eviction, causing long-lived allocations until kernel OOM. Will collect heap/dmesg and driver logs for replay.
Leah Park: good. assign follow-ups: Maddy — kernel/dmesg dump + driver logs to s3://redwood-incident/5950012345/; Sanjay — autoscaler investigation and fix to prevent scale-on-failure loops; Leah — customer communications and postmortem lead.
Sanjay Iyer: putting autoscaler in safe-mode patch: on failure don't immediately attempt scale if recent registration failures >3 in 5m, instead retry cool-off for 10m. I'll open PR and hotpatch.
Maddy Chen: nodes replaced, traffic leveling down, queue length trending down. Current 90th latency still elevated but improving.
Leah Park: handoff: @Sanjay you're primary for the next hour, Maddy on infra follow-ups, I'll coordinate comms. Pager duty will monitor for re-alerts.
PagerDuty: oncall handover noted. Next update requested at 1718501600 (in ~10m).
Sanjay Iyer: monitoring autoscaler, will re-enable once we confirm stable node registration and no Xid churn for 20m. Re-enable command planned: `infra autoscaler update --pool gpu-pool-west-2 --enabled true --min 10 --max 60` but will run only after green.
Maddy Chen: capturing logs:
```
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-5950012345.log
sudo journalctl -u driver-daemon -n 500 > /tmp/driver-5950012345.log
aws s3 cp /tmp/dmesg-5950012345.log s3://redwood-incident/5950012345/
```
Leah Park: thanks team. preliminary impact: ~8 customer tenants experienced >=30% request error increase for 20-50m window. We'll quantify tokens lost and attach to postmortem.
OpsBot: incident state: mitigation in progress, severity -> Sev2 (customer-facing degraded service). Incident owner: Leah Park.
Leah Park: note for postmortem — timeline, decision to pause autoscaler, driver rollback, reserved capacity bump, routing fallback, and follow-ups (autoscaler safe-mode, driver memory regression). Will update main incident doc.
Sanjay Iyer: temporary mitigation successful, queue decreasing, I will keep watch and plan autoscaler re-enable after 20m stable window.
Maddy Chen: decommissioned flapping nodes to debug pool for deeper analysis. grabbing core dumps and driver traces now.
Leah Park: next scheduled update at 1718501600. closing this thread for handoff to oncall ops. Everyone please add any logs/notes to the incident ticket.
OpsBot: thread closed for active messaging at 1718501934 (handoff done).
